what: highlight "the family is the richest family in the world"
said: The richest family in the world does not live in New York or Los Angeles. It comes from a small town in Arkansas.

what: highlight "net worth was estimated to be US$432.4 billion"
said: At the end of twenty twenty-four, the Walton family was worth about four hundred thirty-two billion dollars.

what: highlight "the largest private employer in the world, with 2.1 million employees"
said: Walmart is the biggest private employer on the planet. About two point one million people work there.

what: highlight "the Waltons collectively owned 50.8 percent of Walmart"
said: And the family does not just own a few shares. Back in twenty fourteen, the Waltons owned more than half of the whole company.

what: highlight "With the help of a $20,000 loan"
said: He has about five thousand dollars saved. His wife's father, Leland Robson, lends him twenty thousand more.

what: highlight "it was doing $72,000 in sales, and it increased to $105,000 in the first year"
said: He works hard, cuts prices, and buys in bulk. Sales jump from seventy-two thousand dollars a year to over one hundred thousand in his first year.

what: highlight "It is headquartered in Bentonville, Arkansas ."
said: So the family moved to a tiny town called Bentonville and started over. That is why Walmart is headquartered there today.

what: highlight "The owner of the shop next door refused six times"
said: Even then, it almost did not happen. The shop owner next door refused to give up space six times. Sam's father-in-law quietly went back, paid him, and secured the deal.

what: highlight "the money-strapped young Walton had to learn to delegate responsibility"
said: For a while, Sam ran two stores two hundred twenty miles apart. He could not be in both places, so he had to trust his managers and let them run things.

what: highlight "By 1962, along with his brother Bud, he owned 16 stores"
said: Sam opened more Ben Franklin stores across small towns. By nineteen sixty-two, he and his brother Bud owned sixteen of them.

what: highlight "The first true Walmart opened on July 2, 1962, in Rogers, Arkansas ."
said: On July second, nineteen sixty-two, the first real Walmart opened in Rogers, Arkansas.

what: highlight "there were 125 stores with 7,500 employees and total sales of $340.3 million"
said: By nineteen seventy-five, when Walmart moved into Texas, it had one hundred twenty-five stores and seven thousand five hundred employees.

what: highlight "a $24 million investment linking all stores"
said: Walmart also used technology most stores did not have. In nineteen eighty-seven, it finished a twenty-four million dollar satellite network linking every store to headquarters.

what: highlight "Wal-Mart was more profitable than rivals Kmart and Sears"
said: Bigger rivals like Kmart and Sears were still larger at the time. But Walmart was already making more profit than both of them.

what: highlight "it had become the largest in terms of revenue by October 1989"
said: By October nineteen eighty-nine, Walmart was the largest retailer in America by revenue.

what: highlight "with revenues of $219.8 billion and profits of $6.7 billion"
said: And in two thousand two, it became America's biggest company of any kind, with two hundred nineteen billion dollars in sales.

what: highlight "Walmart is the second-largest company by revenue globally"
said: Today, it is the second-largest company in the world by revenue. And Denise's Saturday dollar is a tiny piece of that river.

what: highlight "convinced him that he should organize his own business as a family partnership"
said: In nineteen fifty-three, long before Walmart existed, Sam's father-in-law gave him one more piece of advice. Run your business as a family partnership.

what: highlight "Sam and Helen owned 20% together while each child owned 20% personally"
said: So the family created a company called Walton Enterprises. Sam and his wife Helen owned twenty percent together. Each of their four children owned twenty percent.

what: highlight "The amount paid out to each person is the same and is agreed upon."
said: All the family's Walmart shares went into that one company. The family made big decisions together, and everyone got paid out the same.

what: highlight "the family accumulated funds in WEI rather than throwing it all over the place"
said: The goal was to keep the money together, instead of letting each child spend it on a fancy life.

what: highlight "besides holding 218 million Walmart common shares"
said: By nineteen eighty-nine, that family company held two hundred eighteen million Walmart shares, plus banks and real estate.

what: highlight "Rob, using his law expertise, helped organize his family's ownership in Walmart into WEI"
said: Sam's oldest son, Rob, was a lawyer. He helped set up the family's ownership this way, and also did the legal work when Walmart went public.

what: highlight "several ultra-wealthy families exploited the GRAT"
said: Rich families today use other legal tools too, like special trusts. Reporters at ProPublica found that some ultra-wealthy families used one kind to avoid billions in estate taxes.

what: highlight "Forbes ranked Sam Walton as the richest person in the United States from 1982 to 1988"
said: Sam Walton became incredibly rich. Forbes named him the richest person in the United States from nineteen eighty-two to nineteen eighty-eight.

what: highlight "Waiting in Line At the Wal-Mart With Everybody Else"
said: But he did not act like it. Newspapers wrote about America's richest man waiting in line at Walmart with everybody else.

what: highlight "the editors began to credit Walton's fortune jointly to him and his four children"
said: In nineteen eighty-nine, Forbes started counting his fortune together with his four children. That alone shows how much the kids already owned.

what: highlight "as tightfisted with money as his father"
said: Sam was also tight with money inside the business. When the family picked a president for Walton Enterprises, they chose his son Jim, because he was just as tightfisted as his father.

what: highlight "In 1992 at the age of 74, Walton died"
said: Sam Walton died in April nineteen ninety-two, at age seventy-four, and was buried in Bentonville.

what: highlight "making her the 18th-richest person and the richest woman in the world"
said: Today, his daughter Alice alone is worth almost ninety billion dollars. In twenty twenty-four, that made her the richest woman in the world.

what: highlight "I pay low wages. I can take advantage of that."
said: Sam Walton was surprisingly honest about this. He once said, I pay low wages. I can take advantage of that.

what: highlight "Walmart was the largest private employer of parents of children enrolled in its program"
said: In two thousand two, a survey in Georgia found Walmart was the largest private employer of parents whose kids were on the state's children's health program.

what: highlight "California taxpayers still pay $86 million a year to Walmart employees"
said: A two thousand four study from Berkeley estimated California taxpayers paid eighty-six million dollars a year in support for Walmart workers.

what: highlight "Walmart insists its wages are generally in line with the current local market in retail labor."
said: Walmart says its wages match what other stores pay in each area. And it has raised pay several times since then.

what: highlight "Walmart's lower prices draw customers away from smaller Main Street businesses"
said: The other big criticism is about towns like Denise's. When a giant store opens on the highway, small shops on Main Street often cannot compete.

what: highlight "Walmart is the largest importer in the United States in many categories"
said: Critics also point to where the products come from. Walmart is the largest importer in the United States in many categories, like electronics.

what: highlight "granted $6.2 billion to approximately 6,300 grantees"
said: The family gives a lot of it away too. In its first thirty years, the Walton Family Foundation gave out six point two billion dollars in grants.

what: highlight "built and curated with $1.2 billion from the foundation"
said: Alice Walton even built a major art museum in Bentonville, with one point two billion dollars from the foundation.
